title: Exposing APIs Safely with API Management
description: Put a policy-driven gateway in front of internal APIs so partners get keys, quotas, and a stable contract.

data.text: Three partner companies need to call your order API. Today you give each of them the same backend URL and an API key baked into a query string. You cannot rate-limit one abusive partner without affecting the others, cannot version the contract without breaking everyone, and cannot audit who called what.

Front the backend with **Azure API Management**. Publish a **versioned API** (`v1`, `v2`) so the contract can evolve, register each partner as a **subscription** with its own key and **rate/quota limits**, and keep the backend URL private. Add policies for JWT validation, caching, and request transformation so the backend stays simple.

data.title: Gateway policies: validate, limit, cache, hide backend
data.code:
<policies>
  <inbound>
    <!-- Reject unauthenticated callers before they reach the backend -->
    <validate-jwt header-name="Authorization" failed-validation-httpcode="401">
      <openid-config url="https://login.microsoftonline.com/{{tenant}}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration" />
      <required-claims>
        <claim name="aud" match="any">
          <value>api://quotient-orders</value>
        </claim>
      </required-claims>
    </validate-jwt>

    <!-- Per-subscription throttling: one abuser cannot starve others -->
    <rate-limit-by-key calls="200" renewal-period="60"
      counter-key="@(context.Subscription?.Id)" />

    <quota-by-key calls="100000" renewal-period="86400"
      counter-key="@(context.Subscription?.Id)" />

    <!-- Serve repeat reads from the gateway cache -->
    <cache-lookup vary-by-developer="true" vary-by-developer-groups="false" />

    <set-backend-service base-url="https://app-quotient-internal.azurewebsites.net" />
  </inbound>

  <backend>
    <forward-request timeout="30" />
  </backend>

  <outbound>
    <cache-store duration="60" />
    <!-- Strip internal headers before returning to the partner -->
    <set-header name="X-Powered-By" exists-action="delete" />
  </outbound>

  <on-error>
    <return-response>
      <set-status code="429" reason="Rate limit exceeded" />
      <set-header name="Retry-After" exists-action="override"><value>60</value></set-header>
    </return-response>
  </on-error>
</policies>

data.title: Backend behind a private endpoint (network isolation)

data.text: Cross-cutting concerns — authentication, throttling, quotas, versioning, logging, transformation — belong in one place rather than reimplemented in every backend. API Management also gives you a **developer portal** where partners self-serve keys, and separates the public contract (`api.example.com/v1/orders`) from internal topology so you can move backends without telling anyone.

cards.title: API Management
pros: Policy engine for auth and transform
cons: Premium tier needed for VNet injection
Gateway adds a small hop latency

cards.title: Application Gateway with WAF
cons: No API keys, versioning, or portal
